summary: Jensen et al. 2017 'New directions in hypnosis research' (Am J Clin Hypn): recommends redirecting resources AWAY from contrasting state vs nonstate positions; high hypnotic suggestibility associated with atypical brain connectivity profiles; clinical efficacy supported.
content: Jensen et al. 2017, 'New directions in hypnosis research: strategies for advancing the cognitive and clinical neuroscience of hypnosis' (PubMed 29034102). Summarizes: (i) clinical research supports hypnosis efficacy for several symptoms/conditions; (ii) research supports role of ACC and prefrontal cortex divisions in hypnotic responding; (iii) emerging finding that high hypnotic suggestibility associated with atypical brain connectivity profiles. Recommendations: strongly consider how hypnotic suggestibility is assessed; include middle-range suggestibility participants; use designs delineating roles of inductions vs specific suggestions. KEY meta-recommendation: redirect resources away from contrasting state and nonstate positions toward (a) efficacy of hypnotic treatments for CNS-influenced conditions, (b) neurophysiological underpinnings of hypnotic phenomena. This is the position many in the field converged on by 2017 and that 2023-2025 work largely operationalizes.
